## Blog: The Real Game of AI Certifications: Hype vs. Practical Skillset

URL: https://fardinraafi.com/blog/ai-certifications-hype-vs-practical-skills · Published 2026-04-28

**TL;DR:** Do AI certifications matter? Why practical workflow-automation skills beat badges, and how to build an AI skillset employers actually want. Career advice.

![AI certifications vs practical AI skills - article cover](https://fardinraafi.com/blogs/blog-2-thumb.webp)

I recently noticed a recurring trend: many of us talk a big game about Generative AI, but when it comes to practical Workflow Optimization or Automation, we often get stuck.

After observing this gap firsthand, I decided to complete 7 back-to-back AI Certification Courses. This learning journey completely opened my eyes to how global platforms are applying core AI concepts in the real world. Today, a traditional degree is simply not enough for students and freshers. You must continuously upgrade yourself to meet market demand, and that is exactly where these free certifications come into play.

## Why Are Certifications Crucial in the AI Era?

The market is more competitive than ever. When you apply for a Marketing, B2B Sales, Business Development, or Growth role, simply labeling yourself an "AI Enthusiast" on your CV won't cut it anymore. Recruiters want hard proof. Having a validated certificate from OpenAI or Google proves that you actually know how to leverage these tools to drive results. It elevates your personal brand instantly.

> "It is incredibly difficult to figure out how to automate complex business processes using Autonomous AI Agents without structured learning. Yes, YouTube is a great resource, but completing a verified certification course completely changes the game."

### 1. OpenAI Academy - AI Foundations & Applied AI Foundations

If you are struggling to understand the root principles and core concepts of Artificial Intelligence, this is the best place to start. There is no substitute for building a strong foundation before diving into practical applications.

 **Key Skills:** AI Principles, Practical Applications.
 **Cost:** Free.
 [View Course ➔](https://academy.openai.com/)

### 2. OpenAI Academy - Agents and Workflows

This was one of my absolute favorite courses. It primarily teaches you how to design Autonomous AI Agents and build automated workflows to run business processes far more efficiently.

 **Key Skills:** Generative AI, Workflow Automation.
 **Cost:** Free.
 [View Course ➔](https://academy.openai.com/)

### 3. Google Digital Academy (Skillshop) - Fundamentals of Digital Marketing

While this is not a pure AI course, it is the global standard for understanding the backbone of digital marketing. Earning this certificate will clear up the basics of marketing data analytics and AI-optimized campaigns.

 **Key Skills:** Digital Marketing, Data Optimization.
 **Cost:** Free.

### 4. Grameenphone Ltd - GenAI & Prompt Engineering

To understand the impact of AI within the local corporate culture, this course by Grameenphone is excellent. It beautifully showcases real-life use cases for advanced Prompt Engineering.

 **Key Skills:** Prompt Engineering, Generative AI.
 **Cost:** Free.
 [View Course ➔](https://www.grameenphone.academy/)

### 5. Grameenphone Ltd - Personal Branding in the AI Era

This course is an excellent guideline on how to maintain your unique value proposition and establish a strong digital presence in the age of AI. You will find fantastic tricks for positioning yourself on your CV and LinkedIn.

 **Key Skills:** Personal Branding, Executive Visibility.
 **Cost:** Free.
 [View Course ➔](https://www.grameenphone.academy/)

### 6. Microsoft & LinkedIn - Career Essentials in Generative AI

This combined certification from Microsoft and LinkedIn is extremely valuable in today's job market. It teaches the ethical usage of AI tools and their application in professional life using very simple language.

 **Key Skills:** Ethical AI, Workplace Productivity.
 **Cost:** Free.
 [View Course ➔](https://www.linkedin.com/learning/topics/professional-certificates)

### 7. HubSpot Academy - AI Marketing Course

If you are a student of marketing or business development, missing out on this course would be a massive mistake. It teaches you exactly how to accelerate your content creation and lead generation processes using AI.

 **Key Skills:** AI Content Strategy, Lead Generation.
 **Cost:** Free.
 [View Course ➔](https://academy.hubspot.com/courses)

## My Personal Advice for Career Growth

Do not just collect certificates for the sake of it. Your main objective should be building a tangible skillset. When you finish a course, actively try to apply that knowledge to a personal project or a volunteer organization. That drive to execute is what will set you apart from everyone else. Remember: AI will not take your job, but a professional who knows how to use AI effectively absolutely will. Still a student? Pair these courses with the free tools in my [.edu mail goldmine guide](https://fardinraafi.com/blog/free-ai-developer-tools-for-students).

What do you think? Are these free certifications making a bigger impact on career growth than traditional institutional education? Let me know your thoughts!

## Blog: The Keyboard is Dying: How AI Voice Dictation is Reshaping Creation and Productivity

URL: https://fardinraafi.com/blog/ai-voice-dictation-keyboard-is-dying · Published 2026-08-18

**TL;DR:** How AI voice dictation tools are reshaping writing, content creation and productivity, and what it means for the future of B2B workflows.

![AI voice dictation replacing the keyboard - article cover](https://fardinraafi.com/blogs/opt/blog-7-1200.webp)

## 🔹 The Unsilent Revolution in Modern Workspaces

For decades, productivity sounded like the clack of mechanical keyboards. Today, that's changing. Walk into a modern tech workspace, and you're just as likely to hear professionals murmuring into microphones and headsets instead of typing.

> Typing is no longer the only gateway from thought to execution. Voice is fast becoming the primary interface for creation.

The driver is AI-powered voice dictation. Modern LLMs and speech-to-text tools no longer need precise, word-for-word input, they can take raw, rambling speech and turn it into polished, structured documentation in seconds.

## 🔹 The Shift: Squeezing Out Keyboard Friction

Historically, typing created a physical latency bottleneck between brain signal and text output. An average professional writes between 40 to 60 words per minute, whereas average human speech ranges between 130 to 160 words per minute. Beyond speed, typing forces an immediate cognitive filter: you must pause, formulate grammar, adjust formatting, and physically press keys to transfer ideas.

### The Power of Stream-of-Consciousness Prompting

AI dictation technology fundamentally alters this dynamic by capturing raw, unstructured thoughts and allowing artificial intelligence to handle the formatting, synthesis, and restructuring.

- **Zero-Friction Brainstorming:** Users can simply vocalize immediate ideas without worrying about spelling or syntax.
- **Instant Synthesis:** LLMs take the raw voice transcript and automatically extract actionable key points, generate structured emails, or draft execution plans.
- **Reduction of Physical Fatigue:** Removing hours of repetitive keyboard interaction significantly decreases physical strain on wrists and hands.

## 🔹 Workplace Dynamics and Hardware Adaptation

While voice-first creation increases individual output, it presents new spatial challenges in shared corporate environments. Open-office floor plans, designed around quiet keyboard usage, are struggling to manage ambient chatter as dozens of team members dictate prompts simultaneously.

### The Rise of Specialized Hardware

To compensate for noise pollution and privacy concerns, a wave of hardware innovation is emerging:

- **Directional Microphones:** Gooseneck and noise-canceling headsets tuned specifically to ignore background chatter and isolate close-range speech.
- **Hardware Mute Pedals:** Programmable foot switches that allow workers to instantly toggle microphone input without interrupting their screen layout.
- **Ambient Soundproofing:** Sound-dampening phone pods and acoustic dividers designed specifically for voice prompting sessions.

What initially appears as an annoying distraction is actually the natural adjustment period between an old workflow standard and a new technological norm.

## 🔹 Speed vs. Depth: The Cognitive Debate

As dictation tools proliferate, researchers and business leaders are evaluating the long-term cognitive implications of abandoning typing.

### The Argument for Deeper Thinking

Critics argue that typing forces an essential mental step: internal editing. When you type, your brain is forced to organize thoughts before they hit the page. Relying entirely on voice-to-AI processing risks replacing active critical thinking with quick, unrefined input, potentially making team members over-reliant on machine synthesis.

### The Argument for Human-Centered Design

Conversely, proponents argue that voice is the most natural human communication medium. Typing was an artificial constraint imposed by early hardware limitations. By allowing professionals to speak naturally, cognitive load is redirected from the physical act of typing to higher-level creative strategy and strategic decision-making.

**Precision vs. Brainstorming:** It is essential to recognize where voice excels and where manual input remains superior.

![Speed vs Depth in AI Voice Dictation](https://fardinraafi.com/blogs/opt/blog-7-img-1200.webp)

## 🔹 Practical Implementation in Daily Workflows

Integrating voice-to-text into daily routines does not require expensive enterprise software overhauls. Most modern operating systems feature robust, built-in speech-to-text engines that can instantly accelerate daily task completion.

> **💡 AI Tip of the Week:** Save time and give your hands a break! Press **Windows + H** anywhere you can type to launch Voice Typing. Simply start speaking, and Windows will convert your words into text in real time. It’s a great way to capture ideas faster, draft emails, or power through documentation with less typing. Give it a try, you might be surprised how quickly it becomes part of your daily workflow!

## 🔹 Conclusion: Adapting to the Voice-First Future

Voice-first creation is not a temporary productivity trend; it represents a fundamental transition in how humans interface with technology. As ambient AI models become quieter, smarter, and more contextually aware, the distinction between "thinking," "speaking," and "executing" will continue to blur.

For business managers, marketers, and technical professionals, mastering voice prompting is fast becoming a core operational skill. Those who learn to combine the speed of voice input with the analytical precision of clear editing will set the standard for modern workplace efficiency.

How is your team handling the transition to AI dictation? Are you embracing voice-first workflows or sticking to traditional typing? Let's connect and discuss!

## Blog: Case Study Series - 1: Brainrot Marketing - The Multi-Million Dollar Growth Playbook

URL: https://fardinraafi.com/blog/brainrot-marketing-case-study · Published 2026-04-12

**TL;DR:** How absurdist internet culture and brainrot marketing drive real brand growth. A case study on Gen Z attention, memes and viral strategy by Fardin Raafi.

![Brainrot marketing case study cover - meme-driven growth strategy](https://fardinraafi.com/blogs/blog-1-thumb.webp)

Think about it for a second. When was the last time you watched a proper, high-budget brand advertisement all the way through?

> Grabbing top-of-funnel attention nowadays is an absolute nightmare. Gen Z's brain filters content so fast that they lose active attention on an ad after just [1.3 seconds](https://www.emarketer.com/content/gen-z-has-1-second-attention-span-work-marketers-advantage).

This is exactly where "Brainrot" marketing has changed the game. It sounds absurd, but this chaotic internet culture is now a multi-million dollar industry. Let's break down the strategies behind it.

## The Strategic Psychology: Why Are Brands Using "Brainrot"?

Brands aren't just acting crazy for no reason. There are three powerful psychological triggers driving this trend:

### 1. The "In-Group" Effect

When a multi-billion-dollar corporation uses a niche meme perfectly, it feels like an inside joke. Gen Z thinks, "Hey, they actually understand our culture!" This builds instant brand affinity.

### 2. Disruptive Pattern Interruption

When we scroll continuously, our brains get used to a pattern. When a completely unhinged video suddenly pops up from a corporate page, we stop scrolling out of pure confusion. That split-second pause is everything.

### 3. Low Production, High Virality

There is no need to spend tons of money on huge agencies or six-figure production budgets. A smart social media manager with a smartphone can generate millions of organic impressions in 24 hours. From an ROI perspective, it is unbelievable!

## The "67" Phenomenon: Capitalizing on Absurdist Culture

One of the craziest trends of 2025 was the "67" brainrot culture. You would be surprised to see how major global companies integrated this trend directly into their marketing pipelines:

**Domino’s Pizza (Conversion & Pricing):** Domino's offered a pizza for exactly $6.70 using the "67" promo code for their loyalty members. This was a masterclass in bottom-of-funnel conversion! They didn't just generate social buzz; they generated direct sales by leveraging a fleeting cultural moment.

**Clash Royale / Supercell (Product-Led Engagement):** When they hit 6.7 million followers on Instagram in October 2025, they didn't just post a boring "Thank You" graphic. Instead, they released a specific "67" in-game emote. It felt more like an inside joke than a promotion, massively boosting user engagement.

**Google (Brand Affinity):** Google quietly dropped an Easter egg. Searching "67" made your screen physically shake, mimicking the hand gesture from the meme. Micro-interactions like this prove that Google stays culturally updated.

## Duolingo's "Skibidi Toilet" & Lore Era

Duolingo’s marketing team plays the game on a whole different level.

They don't just use memes, they turned internet subculture into their core brand identity. Their mascot, Duo the Owl, participates in the "Skibidi Toilet" trend, picks fake corporate fights on TikTok, and acts like an obsessed pop-star fanboy.

The impact? They completely bypassed ad-blockers. Gen Z now actively searches for Duolingo ads just for entertainment. And that is exactly how they maintain their spot as the top-grossing education app globally.

## Bangladesh is Not Lagging Behind! (Local Masterclasses)

We are seeing some brilliant implementations of this culture right here in the local market.

### 1. Chorki (Community-Led Cult Marketing)

Chorki is arguably the pioneer in bringing this culture to the mainstream in Bangladesh. During the release of "Myself Allen Swapan," they officially partnered with Facebook's biggest local meme community, Rantages.

Later, during the film "Utshob," they released highly specific meme templates. Templates hitting pain points like IELTS struggles or engineering academic pressure resonated deeply with students. The audience unknowingly generated massive organic promotional reach for Chorki.

### 2. bKash (Cultural Hijacking & Seasonal Virality)

bKash knows exactly how to hijack a cultural moment and let the internet do the marketing for them.

Their Eid tagline was literally designed to function as a meme template. Every Eid, the younger generation creates aggressive and funny memes with it, tagging elders to ask for Eidi (Salami). This is a textbook example of using top-of-funnel internet humor to drive bottom-of-the-funnel conversions (peer-to-peer money transfers).

## The Bottom Line?

> Brainrot marketing is not just about making stupid content. It is a highly calculated psychological framework that dictates when, where, and how to hack the audience's attention and convert it into measurable growth.

**Next in the series:** [Case Study Series - 2: Warid to Cirkle](https://fardinraafi.com/blog/warid-to-cirkle-rebrand-case-study)

## Blog: ChatGPT Ads Just Crossed $1 Billion: The End of Keywords and the Future of AI Marketing

URL: https://fardinraafi.com/blog/chatgpt-ads-future-of-ai-marketing · Published 2026-09-14

**TL;DR:** ChatGPT Ads and conversational advertising: why context-based AI ads could replace keyword marketing, and what marketers should do now.

![ChatGPT Ads and the future of AI marketing - article cover](https://fardinraafi.com/blogs/opt/blog-8-1200.webp)

The digital marketing landscape is experiencing a tectonic shift. ChatGPT Ads just crossed the $1 billion revenue mark in less than 200 days after launch. This number is staggering, but the revenue itself is not the most interesting part of the story.

The truly fascinating element is the fundamental change in how digital advertising will operate moving forward. Google gives us a list of search results. Instagram provides an endless visual feed. ChatGPT, however, gives us a fluid conversation.

Brands now have the unprecedented opportunity to advertise in an environment where users are actively exploring options, comparing specific products, asking for customized recommendations, and making high-stakes decisions. With the ChatGPT Ads Manager now available for self-serve advertising in regions like India, we are witnessing the opening chapter of a completely new playbook.

But before you reallocate your entire marketing budget, we need to look at the reality of the platform today and what this means for the broader artificial intelligence ecosystem.

## 🔹 The Early Stage Reality Check for Advertisers

The hype surrounding this launch is massive. However, looking under the hood of the early beta access reveals a platform that is still in its infancy.

Right now, the system lacks the robust optimization infrastructure that growth marketers rely on. We are currently limited to basic "Reach" campaigns. There is no conversion tracking pixel. There is no ability to retarget users who engaged with your brand previously. The reporting metrics are incredibly basic.

If you approach ChatGPT Ads expecting it to function like a mature Meta or Google Ads dashboard that will instantly drop your Customer Acquisition Cost, you will fail. It is a raw ecosystem.

My recommendation for growth teams and business development leaders is clear. Treat this as a strategic experiment. Allocate 5 to 10 percent of your budget to testing if you have access. Keep the vast majority of your capital deployed on proven, measurable channels until the OpenAI advertising infrastructure matures.

## 🔹 The Biggest Mindset Shift: From Keywords to Moments

Despite the current technical limitations, the long-term potential is revolutionary because of one singular factor: **search-like intent.**

This is not the passive, interruption-based intent of social media scrolling. People are literally typing their highly specific business and personal problems into the chat interface in real time.

The biggest required mindset shift for marketers is to stop obsessing over exact-match keywords and start thinking about critical moments. You must ask yourself what specific conversations your brand needs to appear in.

### Strategies for Conversational Targeting

Instead of bidding on generic terms, forward-thinking brands are already testing highly contextual strategies:

- **Competitor Conversations:** Positioning your brand strategically when a user asks the AI to compare your biggest rival to other market alternatives.
- **Problem-Centric Prompts:** Appearing exactly when a user describes a pain point that your specific software or service was built to solve.
- **Persona-Based Buying Questions:** Engaging when decision-makers ask highly technical questions about implementation, pricing, or resource scaling.
- **High-Intent Educational Moments:** Providing immediate, branded value when users ask the AI to explain a complex industry concept.

### What This Means for the Broader AI Ecosystem

OpenAI proving that conversational advertising is not only viable but highly lucrative will send shockwaves through the entire artificial intelligence industry. The compute costs required to run Large Language Models are astronomical. Subscription tiers alone cannot sustain the massive scale these companies are targeting.

Here is what we can expect to happen across the landscape:

- **The Rush to Monetize Free Tiers:** Competitors like [Claude](https://fardinraafi.com/blog/claude-sonnet-5-agentic-ai) and Gemini will face immense pressure to follow suit. While Perplexity has already stepped into the AI search advertising space, traditional conversational models will need to find ways to monetize their massive free user bases. Ad-supported free tiers will likely become the absolute industry standard within the next twelve months.
- **The Evolution of Native AI Formats:** Right now, we are thinking about ads in traditional terms. But AI models will soon pioneer entirely new formats. Imagine dynamic product feeds generated directly inside the chat window based on the user's specific problem. We will see interactive widgets, real-time CRM integrations, and direct booking systems embedded seamlessly into the AI's natural response.
- **A Direct Threat to Traditional Search Hegemony:** Google has held a monopoly on intent-based advertising for decades. But context-based AI advertising is far more natural and highly personalized. If users can get a perfectly tailored product recommendation complete with an embedded purchasing option through a simple conversation, the traditional process of scrolling through ten blue links will feel instantly outdated.

## 🔹 The Future Belongs to Context

The transition from keyword-based advertising to context-based advertising is officially underway. The brands that learn how to navigate conversational targeting early will build a massive, almost insurmountable advantage over the next few years.

They will capture high-intent users at a fraction of the cost of legacy channels. They will build trust by appearing as helpful solutions in moments of genuine need, rather than as intrusive banners on a webpage.

The technology is evolving rapidly, and consumer behavior is shifting right alongside it. The only question left for modern marketers and business leaders is this:

> Can your brand become part of the conversation?

---

## Blog: Claude Sonnet 5: The Era of 'Agentic' AI and What It Means for You

URL: https://fardinraafi.com/blog/claude-sonnet-5-agentic-ai · Published 2026-07-21

**TL;DR:** What does "agentic AI" mean? How Claude Sonnet 5 and AI agents change B2B growth, marketing automation and everyday work, explained simply.

![Claude Sonnet 5 and agentic AI - article cover](https://fardinraafi.com/blogs/opt/blog-6-1200.webp)

It feels like a new AI model is released every single week. We try it out, write a few prompts, and then go right back to our old workflows.

But the release of Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5 is different. One specific word was highly emphasized in their announcement: *"Agentic"*.

So, what does this actually mean for you? What is the real meaning behind the word "Agentic"?

## From Chat Assistant to Autonomous Agent

Previously, we asked AI to draft an email or summarize a topic, and the job ended there.

Agentic AI means the model does not just sit there after answering a single prompt. If you give it a broad task, it will plan the steps, complete multiple actions, and execute an entire workflow on its own.

> In simple words, it’s not just a chat assistant anymore, it’s an **autonomous agent**.

## The Impact on B2B Growth and Marketing

For professionals working in B2B marketing, lead generation, or CRM data, this is a massive opportunity. Let’s look at what we can practically do with it:

### 1. B2B Automation & CRM Data Hygiene

The biggest pain point in lead generation is messy data. Manually cleaning thousands of raw leads exported from Apollo.io or Salesforce takes hours. Now, you can instruct Claude Sonnet to clean, filter, and enrich this data with extreme accuracy. It will automatically sort the data according to your Ideal Customer Profile (ICP).

### 2. Building Complex AI Chatbots

You can now build advanced AI chatbots for your website or clients without heavy coding knowledge. Older models would lose track of long conversations, but Sonnet’s improved reasoning capacity makes it perfect for complex customer support and lead qualification tasks.

### 3. Deep Market Research & Competitor Analysis

The days of manual competitor analysis are almost over. Give the AI a specific framework, and it will browse multiple sources to generate a ready-made, actionable report. It can find out competitor pricing or feature gaps and present everything to you in a perfectly structured format.

### 4. Managing the B2B Supply Chain of Leads

I always say (more on this in [Selling is 80% Psychology](https://fardinraafi.com/blog/selling-is-80-percent-psychology)) that B2B outreach is like a supply chain, and reducing bottlenecks is crucial. With Agentic AI, you can drastically reduce your sales cycle latency. It can handle multiple steps entirely on its own, from initial prospect research to deep email personalization.

## The Paradigm Shift

The AI game is no longer just about "which model writes better." The landscape has completely shifted.

> The new competition is: **"Which model can finish the job for you on its own."**

Professionals who adapt to these autonomous workflows today will be the ones leading the job market tomorrow.

---

## Blog: Master Your LinkedIn Profile: Your Personal Brand

URL: https://fardinraafi.com/blog/linkedin-profile-optimization-personal-brand · Published 2026-06-30

**TL;DR:** A practical LinkedIn profile optimization guide: headline, banner, about section and content that attract recruiters and inbound opportunities.

![LinkedIn profile optimization and personal branding guide cover](https://fardinraafi.com/blogs/opt/blog-5-1200.webp)

Think practically for a moment. You apply for a job, and what is the very first thing HR does after looking at your CV? In 99% of cases, they will search your name on LinkedIn.

This is your digital first impression. And you only get one shot to make it right.

> Your LinkedIn profile is not just an online CV. **It is your 24/7 personal brand,** working for you even while you sleep.

**The Goal:** Attract the right opportunities, the right people, and meaningful conversations.
 **The Reality:** Most profiles out there are incomplete, generic, and completely invisible to recruiters.

So, how do you break out of this invisible zone? Here are 4 practical steps to optimize your profile today:

## 1. Strong Headline: Be specific on value, not just your title

Most people simply write "Marketing Executive" or "Student at XYZ University" in their headline. This is a huge mistake!

Instead of stating your position, tell people what you *do* for them.

Instead of "Marketing Executive", try writing: *"I help FMCG brands grow through data-driven campaigns."*

**Pro Tip:** If your headline is just your job title, you are missing a massive opportunity to make profile visitors curious.

## 2. Clear About Section: Write like a human, not a robot

What does your profile say about you within the first 5 seconds of a visit?

When people see a bio packed with corporate jargon (e.g., "highly motivated, detail-oriented individual"), they instantly scroll past. No one wants to connect with a robot.

Always write your About section in the first person. Keep the tone conversational. Talk about your career journey, your vision, and your passions. Finally, make sure to include a clear Call to Action (CTA) at the end. For example: *"Open to new B2B growth opportunities, let's connect over a virtual coffee."*

Simple Rule: If you cannot read what you wrote naturally out loud, rewrite it.

## 3. Featured Section: Show, Don't Just Tell (Bonus Tip!)

Your headline and About section tell people your story, but where is the proof?

This is where the Featured section comes in. Use it to visually pin your best projects, portfolio links, media features, or awards. For example, I use mine to showcase my ISCEA Global Case Competition achievements and my TEDx volunteering work. Doing this instantly boosts your credibility.

## 4. Consistent Activity: Hiding keeps you forgotten

> Hiding from LinkedIn doesn't keep you safe, it keeps you forgotten.

If you set everything up perfectly but remain completely inactive on LinkedIn, it won't help you.

Try to post about an industry-related topic at least once a week. Leave valuable comments on posts made by your target audience or Key Decision Makers (KDMs). When those conversations turn into calls, the tips in [Selling is 80% Psychology](https://fardinraafi.com/blog/selling-is-80-percent-psychology) take over. Over time, this consistency will build your visibility and establish trust.

Do you know what the result will be? You won't have to chase every single opportunity yourself; recruiters and collaborators will start sending inbound messages to you!

**Ready to build your profile?**
 The difference between a great LinkedIn profile and a generic one dictates whether your career will rapidly grow or stay stuck in one place.

## Blog: Selling is 80% Psychology & 20% Product Knowledge: Where is Your Focus?

URL: https://fardinraafi.com/blog/selling-is-80-percent-psychology · Published 2026-06-09

**TL;DR:** Why B2B sales is mostly psychology: stop feature-dumping, diagnose the real problem and close more deals. Practical B2B sales lessons by Fardin Raafi.

![Selling is 80% psychology - B2B sales article cover](https://fardinraafi.com/blogs/opt/blog-4-1200.webp)

Early in my career, while working on B2B outreach and lead generation, I made a very common mistake. I genuinely believed that if I could just perfectly explain every single feature of our product or service to the client, the deal would automatically close.

But reality hit me fast. I noticed that even when my product knowledge was at 100%, deals were still slipping through my fingers. The reason? I was completely ignoring the psychology behind the sale.

> No one warned me early on that B2B selling is actually **80% psychology and only 20% product knowledge!**

## Pushy vs. Persuasive: What is the Real Difference?

Often, in a rush to hit our targets, we unintentionally become pushy. This pushy attitude is the biggest bottleneck in any good sales process.

**The Pushy Rep says:** "Buy now or miss out!"

**The Persuasive Rep says:** "Here is what solving this specific problem looks like for you."

To a pushy salesperson, a client's "No" just means they need to try harder. Conversely, to a persuasive salesperson, a "No" means they need to pause and understand *why*.

## Feature Dumping vs. Problem Solving

The biggest invisible habit destroying your close rate in the B2B sales cycle is "Feature Dumping."

Feature-focused reps only pitch what their product can do. Problem-focused reps, however, focus entirely on the pain the client is experiencing by *not* having the solution.

Statistics show that [67% of lost sales](https://www.zippia.com/advice/sales-statistics/) happen because the salesperson never properly qualified the buyer or understood their actual needs. Silence from a prospect indicates an unmet pain point, and talking over them continuously only results in a missed diagnosis.

## How I Close the Gap (Practical Moves)

So, how do you close this gap? The answer isn't to push harder; it is to understand more deeply. Here are a few actionable tips straight from my regular Business Development workflow:

### 1. Discovery Questions

Start your calls with at least two solid discovery questions. Give the client the floor to talk.

### 2. Mirroring

Instead of reciting a memorized script, mirror the language and terminology that the client uses.

### 3. Post-Meeting Summary

Send a "What I heard" or summary email immediately after the meeting. This works like magic to build trust and alignment.

## The Mindset Shift

You might use tools like **Salesforce** or **Apollo.io** to identify the perfect Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) or Key Decision Maker (KDM), but at the end of the day, conversion relies entirely on your follow-up execution and your mindset.

> You might be surprised to learn that [79% of marketing leads never convert](https://blog.hubspot.com/blog/tabid/6307/bid/30901/30-thought-provoking-lead-nurturing-stats-you-can-t-ignore.aspx), mostly due to poor follow-up and a lack of lead nurturing!

Change your mindset starting today:

- **Rejection** does not mean failure.
- **Curiosity** is far more important than persuasion.
- **Trust** takes time to build, and that is completely okay.

A lost deal doesn't mean your product is bad. It just means the connection wasn't there. Remember, the salespeople who consistently win are the ones who sell *with* the client, not *at* them.

---

## Blog: Case Study Series - 2: Warid to Cirkle: Identity Crisis or Strategic Evolution?

URL: https://fardinraafi.com/blog/warid-to-cirkle-rebrand-case-study · Published 2026-11-27

**TL;DR:** Warid, Airtel, Robi and now Cirkle: a Bangladesh telecom rebrand case study on borrowed brand equity, switching costs and youth positioning by Fardin Raafi.

![Warid to Airtel to Cirkle rebrand case study - article cover](https://fardinraafi.com/blogs/opt/blog-10-1200.webp)

Think about it. One SIM card, one 016 number, and four different names on the screen in under twenty years. Warid. Airtel. Airtel by Robi. And now, Cirkle.

Most brands spend decades trying to build one name people trust. This one kept changing its name and kept its customers anyway. A name can change four times. The number in your pocket never did, and that is the whole story.

So is this a brand that never knew who it was? Or one of the smartest long games in Bangladeshi telecom? Let's break it down.

### 1. Warid: the fastest start in the market (2007)

Warid Telecom, owned by the UAE based Abu Dhabi Group, paid [US$50 million for Bangladesh's sixth mobile licence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warid_Bangladesh) in December 2005 and went live on [10 May 2007](https://archive.thedailystar.net/2007/05/10/d70510050257.htm).

The launch was aggressive. Warid hit [1 million subscribers in 70 days](https://today.thefinancialexpress.com.bd/print/warid-telecom-achieves-10m-active-subscribers-in-70-days) and was the [fourth largest operator in two years](https://www.zawya.com/en/business/warid-secures-25m-subscribers-in-bangladesh-q3ou0snm). Big network, fast growth, but a late entrant fighting giants. That gap is what made the next move happen.

### 2. Airtel: borrowing a global name (2010)

In 2010, [Bharti Airtel bought 70% of Warid for $300 million](https://observerbd.com/news/588596) and the brand became Airtel.

This was a classic borrowed equity play. Instead of building trust from zero, you plug into a name that already means something across South Asia and Africa. Airtel then did the local work itself, positioning hard on youth, cheap data and "friends" culture. Over 16 years, it became one of the few telecom brands young people actually felt something for.

### 3. Airtel by Robi: the awkward decade (2016 to 2026)

In 2016, Airtel merged with Robi. Legally it became one company. But Robi did something smart: it [kept Airtel alive as its youth sub-brand](https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-technology/60-consumer-ecosystems/20699-robi-axiata-drops-airtel-youth-brand-renames-it-cirkle.html), on the same network.

Two brands, one infrastructure. Robi for the mass market, Airtel for the young. Smart segmentation, but it came with a catch.

Grameenphone and Banglalink [complained to the regulator](https://www.thedailystar.net/business/news/robi-faces-complaints-gp-banglalink-over-airtel-branding-4038041) that Robi's continued use of the Airtel name broke the 2016 merger conditions, one of which required marketing under the Robi name. Robi said the matter was fully resolved and approved. Still, when you are renting a name you don't own, someone can always question the lease.

### 4. Cirkle: owning the house instead of renting it (2026)

On [17 August 2026](https://observerbd.com/news/588523), Robi officially retired Airtel and launched Cirkle. Same 016 numbers, same SIMs, same balances, same packages. Only the identity changed.

Robi frames it as the [next step for a young, digital first generation](https://en.ittefaq.com.bd/17765/airtel-now-robi-%E2%80%98cirkle%E2%80%99), with more focus on affordable digital services and AI.

Here is the part most people miss. The name "Airtel" always belonged to someone else. Cirkle belongs to Robi. Every taka spent building it now builds Robi's own asset, not a partner's.

It also echoes Airtel's own old tagline, the network of friends. A circle of friends. The memory carries over even when the logo doesn't.

## The marketer's take

If you work in branding, this case gives you three practical lessons:

- **Protect the switching cost, not the logo.** Cirkle kept every 016 number. Customers lost nothing, so there was no reason to leave. If your rebrand asks users to do work, you will lose some of them.
- **Borrowed equity has an expiry date.** Licensing a big name helps you start fast. But at some point you are building someone else's brand with your budget. Plan the exit early.
- **A new name doesn't fix an old experience.** According to BTRC data, Robi received [the most complaints of the four operators](https://observerbd.com/news/589530) between January 2021 and June 2026. A fresh logo gets attention. Only better service keeps it.

Globally, we've seen this before. Dunkin' dropped "Donuts" from its name to signal it was more than one product. It worked because the coffee was already there. The rebrand followed the reality, not the other way around. (I broke down another culture-first brand move in [why brands pay to get roasted](https://fardinraafi.com/blog/why-brands-pay-to-get-roasted).)

## So, identity crisis or strategic evolution?

Honestly? Both, depending on when you looked.

From 2016 to 2026, it did look like an identity crisis. Two brands on one network, a name owned by a shareholder, and competitors questioning whether it was even allowed.

But Cirkle is the move that resolves it. It turns a borrowed name into an owned one while keeping the one thing customers actually cared about, their number.

The strategy is sound. The real test is not the logo launch at Sonargaon. It is whether a 20 year old in Rajshahi gets better data speed next month.

So what do you think? Is Cirkle a fresh start, or just a new jacket on the same network? Catch up on [Case Study Series - 1: Brainrot Marketing](https://fardinraafi.com/blog/brainrot-marketing-case-study) too.

---

## Blog: Modern Marketing: Why Are Brands Paying to Get Roasted?

URL: https://fardinraafi.com/blog/why-brands-pay-to-get-roasted · Published 2026-05-19

**TL;DR:** Why modern brands pay creators to roast them, and how culture-led, self-aware marketing wins Gen Z attention. Brand strategy insights by Fardin Raafi.

![Brands paying to get roasted - culture-led marketing article cover](https://fardinraafi.com/blogs/opt/blog-3-1200.webp)

Think about it. We don't have the patience to watch a 5-second ad on YouTube. We literally sit with our fingers hovering over the mouse, eagerly waiting for the "Skip" button to appear.

Yet, those same people will happily sit down to watch a 2-hour roast show where the sponsor brands are ruthlessly made fun of! And the crazy part? Brands are paying top dollar just to be insulted.

> This is what I call **Modern Marketing**. It sounds absurd, but the game of product marketing has completely shifted.

## The Power Shift: Who Holds the Control Now?

Once upon a time, brands had full control over the narrative. They produced highly polished videos, wrote perfect scripts, and bought our attention with feature-heavy product pitches. But the tables have turned. Today, the power belongs entirely to the audience.

Gen Z and modern internet audiences absolutely despise the traditional corporate monologue. If your content feels even slightly "promotional" or fake, they will scroll past it in a microsecond. They don't come online to listen to brand lectures; they come to enjoy the moment.

## Case Study: India’s Got Latent

### Samay Raina & Internet Culture

Take Samay Raina’s [India’s Got Latent](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=India%27s+Got+Latent) as a prime example. Premiering across YouTube and Netflix, it has taken the internet by storm.

Why is this show so incredibly popular? Because it is raw, unpredictable, and perfectly aligned with meme culture. Startup founders come onto the show specifically to get roasted. Brands become part of the inside jokes. People don't view these integrations as advertisements; they share them organically as pure entertainment.

## Influencer Marketing vs. Culture-Led Marketing

If this sounds familiar, it is the same psychology I broke down in [Brainrot Marketing](https://fardinraafi.com/blog/brainrot-marketing-case-study). Many marketers might brush this off as just another influencer marketing strategy. It is not. This is **culture-led marketing**! When you successfully integrate your product into an active trend or culture, people start viewing your brand as an extension of their own identity.

> You can no longer earn attention just by shouting "We are the best." Attention is earned when you naturally become part of an interesting conversation.

## The Ultimate Framework for Modern Attention

If your brand wants to survive and thrive in this era, you have to break some old rules:

### 1. Stop the Corporate Monologue

Consumers do not care about your list of product features. They care about relevance.

### 2. Be Interesting Enough to Share

Do something bold that makes people want to create memes about you and discuss your brand in their private group chats.

### 3. Embrace the Raw Format

An authentic, unpolished, and raw approach is far more effective today than a perfectly manicured corporate aesthetic.

Truth be told, the very definition of marketing has evolved. Marketing no longer means interrupting people's entertainment to show an ad.

Marketing itself must become the entertainment.
